The officials were still discussing whether the shot had been made in ____3____. My excitement had moved faster than the decision. I needed to wait for the ____4____ result, not choose the version supported by the loudest ____5____.

The pause felt long. Someone called out for me to get on with it. I explained briefly that confirmation was still needed. The microphone could carry useful information, but it could also spread an unconfirmed ____6____ to the whole hall. A minute later, the officials gave the score. The late shot did not count. I read the confirmed numbers without adding my own ____7____. One team was disappointed, yet its players knew the decision had come from the officials rather than the person with the ____8____. Afterwards, the teacher thanked me for keeping the roles ____9____. I had not judged the play; I had communicated the judgement when it was ____10____.
